title: Adaptive Context Anchors for Multi-Workspace Route Lattice
creator: Marina Gomez
description: Problem: as customers add more workspaces and product surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost views, model routes), the console sidebar becomes noisy and switching contexts loses state. This ticket defines a route-centric information architecture: a Route Lattice that maps workspace anchors to surface roots, and an adaptive left rail that surfaces contextual anchors, quick-jump chips, and persistent last-view state per workspace. Goals: reduce time-to-target for engineers by 30%, preserve per-workspace rollouts and dashboard state during switches, surface cost and SLA indicators inline, and keep keyboard-first navigation intact. Scope: IA changes (routing + persisted tabs), left-rail micro-patterns (collapsible anchors, overflow behavior), workspace-switcher affordances (recent, pinned, role-aware), and prototype handoff to engineering with telemetry events for metrics. Out of scope for this ticket: backend routing implementation details and Dedicated/private deployment-specific RBAC rules (separate ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Left rail renders workspace anchors (3 max visible) and collapses extras into an overflow menu
Switching workspaces preserves last-opened surface (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) per workspace
Keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens a quick-jump palette that resolves to Route Lattice targets with fuzzy match
Cost badges and SLA micro-indicators appear inline on anchors and update via Console telemetry
Prototype reviewed and signed off by PM & Eng with annotated Figma frames and implementation notes
decisions: Use a Route Lattice (graph of root routes) instead of deep nested menus to reduce cognitive load; each anchor maps to a canonical route
Persist last-active pane per workspace (tradeoff: increased client-side state vs improved UX); decided to add lightweight local storage keyed by workspace ID
Limit visible anchors to 3 on small screens and surface an overflow menu instead of horizontal scrolling to improve accessibility
Show cost and SLA micro-indicators on anchors (low-fidelity badges) rather than full cost numbers to avoid noise; dashboard will still show detailed cost breakdowns
Prefer keyboard-first quick-jump palette integration before adding an extra top-nav search to keep UI minimal
tasks: Finalize annotated Figma frames with component specs and responsive rules
Create a lightweight design token map for anchor badges (colors, sizes, aria labels)
Work with Eng to define telemetry events: workspace_switch, anchor_click, quick_jump_selection
Prototype accessibility states (focus, expanded/condensed, screen-reader labels) and run AX checklist
Prepare handoff doc with edge-cases and fallback behavior for offline/slow connections
